_comment: Mutations that break the Google REDIRECT sign-in flow, one at a time.
Every mutation must be caught by frontend/src/__tests__/googleRedirectSignIn.test.tsx.
This spec has no pytest target: the flow is front-end only and its tests
are run by vitest. The harness accepts a 'command' for exactly that case,
and keeps every other guarantee it already had -- snapshot before, SHA-256
revert verification after, and a SKIP counts as a failure.
The server half of the same flow (single-use enforcement, and the rule
that a credential is never logged) is a SEPARATE spec with a pytest
NEVER run concurrently with a test run or tools/review_fanout.py -- both will
read a file that is mid-mutation and report on code that does not exist.

mutations.label: A: the redirect URI gains a trailing slash (Google rejects it with redirect_uri_mismatch)
mutations.replace: export const GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI = "https://depthsight.diverseinc.net/";  // MUTANT

mutations.label: B: the flow asks for an auth code, so no credential ever arrives in the fragment
mutations.replace: response_type: "code",  // MUTANT

mutations.label: C: the email scope is dropped
mutations.replace: export const GOOGLE_SCOPE = "openid profile";  // MUTANT

mutations.label: D: the browser is sent somewhere other than Google's authorization endpoint
mutations.replace:
export const GOOGLE_AUTHORIZE_ENDPOINT =
	"https://example.invalid/o/oauth2/v2/auth";  // MUTANT

mutations.label: E: the credential is left in the address bar and in the browser history
F: the handler stops checking that the credential belongs to this sign-in request
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: neither a missing marker nor a foreign state is rejected

mutations.label: G: the credential is posted to the wrong endpoint
mutations.replace: const response = await fetch("/api/v1/auth/token", {  // MUTANT

mutations.label: H: the credential is sent under the wrong body key
mutations.replace: credential: submission.token,  // MUTANT

mutations.label: I: the handler never forwards the credential, so nobody is signed in
J: the failure path is silent, so a broken sign-in looks like a normal page load
K: a redirect that comes back without a credential is not reported
mutations.replace:
// MUTANT: the missing credential is not reported
			return;

mutations.label: L: the handler is not mounted, so the sign-in cannot complete on the site root
mutations.replace: {/* MUTANT: the handler is not mounted */}

mutations.label: M: the button does not remember the sign-in request, so the credential cannot be verified
mutations.replace: if (false) {  // MUTANT: the sign-in request is not remembered

mutations.label: N: the age of the request rejects a credential whose state MATCHES (the slow-user bug)
mutations.replace:
const at = typeof parsed.at === "number" ? parsed.at : 0;
	if (Date.now() - at > PENDING_MAX_AGE_MS) return null;  // MUTANT: an aged marker is dropped

mutations.label: O: the state is not compared at all, so a foreign response is accepted
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the state is never compared

mutations.label: P: a missing marker is reported as an unverified credential instead of a sign-in that took too long
mutations.replace: fail(t("googleSignInUnverified"));  // MUTANT: the wrong message

mutations.label: R: a stale marker makes an unrelated later visit report a sign-in failure
mutations.replace: if (false) {  // MUTANT: a stale marker is treated as fresh

mutations.label: S: the marker is not written to the SHARED store, so a sign-in that comes back in another tab is rejected
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the marker is not written to the shared store

mutations.label: T: the SHARED store is never read, so a sign-in that comes back in another tab is rejected
mutations.replace: sharedRaw = null;  // MUTANT: the shared store is never read

mutations.label: U: a browser that blocks storage is not reported, so the sign-in fails in silence
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: an unavailable storage is not reported

mutations.label: V: the sign-in starts even when the marker cannot be recorded, so it is guaranteed to be rejected on the way back
mutations.replace: if (!rememberPendingGoogleRequest(googleSignIn.state) && false) {

mutations.label: W: the claim never refuses a second attempt, so a reload sends the credential twice
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the claim never refuses a second attempt

mutations.label: X: the one-time value is not sent to the server, so the server cannot consume it once
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the one-time value is not sent

mutations.label: Y: every attempt carries the SAME one-time value, so the server refuses the user's second attempt
mutations.replace: nonce: "the-same-one-time-value",  // MUTANT

mutations.label: Z: a new attempt does not supersede the previous claim, so the user cannot sign in again
mutations.replace: // MUTANT: the previous claim is never superseded
